extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Department of Education Federal financial assistance (postsecondary institutions, elementary and secondary schools), Title IX coordinators, institutional legal counsel, and policymakers implementing Title IX regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble guidance and interpretive explanations accompanying the Department of Education's Final Title IX regulations, describing legal scope, implementation expectations, enforcement practices, and related administrative matters for recipients and enforcement officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory justification despite limited empirical data; consideration of qualitative benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department may promulgate regulations based on review of case law, enforcement experience, and stakeholder feedback even where extensive empirical datasets are limited; Executive Order 12866 and OMB Circular A-4 direct agencies to consider qualitative benefits as essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are not required to produce extensive empirical evidence before acting—prophylactic rules are permissible. The Department cites qualitative benefits (e.g., improvements to psychological wellbeing) as support for regulation. See Stilwell v. Off. of Thrift Supervision and Executive Order 12866 guidance; detailed costs and benefits are discussed in the Regulatory Impact Analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for long-lasting, flexible regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations should be balanced, widely acceptable, provide clarity and settled expectations, and offer flexibility to be implemented across diverse postsecondary institutions and education settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations should promote stability in enforcement, aid recipients in setting expectations and ensuring accountability, and offer reasonable flexibility so institutions can address sex discrimination while meeting Title IX obligations. Simplicity and clarity are desirable to limit frequent disruptive updates; the Department retained provisions from the 2020 amendments where appropriate (e.g., supportive measures, prohibiting bias/conflicts of interest, consolidation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of intersection with other laws and agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations apply to recipients of Department funding; other Federal agencies may have their own Title IX or related nondiscrimination regulations, and recipients may need to comply with multiple agencies' implementing rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department confirms these final regulations apply only to Department recipients and do not condition other agencies' funding on compliance with this Department's regulations. Recipients that receive assistance from multiple agencies should comply with each agency's applicable Title IX implementing regulations; the Department does not intend these regulations to create conflicts with other agencies' rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family Policymaking Assessment consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters requested a Family Policymaking Assessment per the Treasury and General Government Appropriations Act of 1999; the Department reviewed applicable requirements and determined the regulations apply to recipients rather than directly to families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must consider impacts on family well-being where applicable; the Department states it has reviewed and complied with applicable requirements in promulgating these regulations because the rules regulate recipients of Federal financial assistance rather than families directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection regardless of national origin, immigration status; threats of deportation as retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX protections apply to individuals irrespective of national origin, immigration status, or citizenship; threatening deportation or invoking immigration status to intimidate or deter a Title IX complaint may constitute retaliation under Title IX if done to interfere with a protected activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retaliation is defined in §§ 106.2 and 106.71; threatening deportation or intimidation based on immigration status falls within that definition when purposefully used to interfere with rights under Title IX, so additional regulatory language was deemed unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of employment under Title IX
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX applies to any person (including employees) in an education program or activity receiving Department Federal financial assistance; the statute is not limited to students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These final regulations continue the longstanding application of Title IX to employment contexts that occur under a recipient's education program or activity. Nothing in these regulations derogates employee rights under Title VII nor precludes employers from complying with Title VII; institutions must satisfy obligations under both statutes as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding for compliance is recipient responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX imposes obligations on recipients but does not appropriate funds to cover compliance costs; the Department's final regulations clarify legal obligations but do not provide funding mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients that realize costs due to the final regulations must identify funding sources independently (e.g., Congress appropriates funds, not Title IX itself). The Regulatory Impact Analysis contains a detailed discussion of costs and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of technical assistance to support implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will offer technical assistance to recipients (including sample policies, procedures, training materials, checklists, and webinars) and provide guidance on interactions with other laws (FERPA, Equal Access Act, Title VI, IDEA, Section 504) as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR encourages Title IX Coordinators and others to contact OCR via provided links for questions. Equity Assistance Centers provide training and assistance on nondiscrimination areas; Student Privacy Policy Office handles FERPA questions. Technical assistance is intended to reduce burdens, especially for smaller or less-resourced recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intra-agency and interagency coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will coordinate within its offices and with other Federal agencies (e.g., DOJ) on programs with overlapping purposes (e.g., VAWA 2022, Clery Act) to promote consistency and more efficient implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive Order 12250 directs coordination; the Department will share data when appropriate and work with Federal partners to promote consistent enforcement while noting the final regulations apply only to Department recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology to ensure broad coverage ('person' vs. specific labels)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations use the term 'person' to ensure Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate applies to anyone in a recipient's education program or activity; terms like 'applicant', 'student', or 'employee' are used to require particular recipient actions, not to narrow application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the regulations use narrower terms, they do so to trigger specific procedural or substantive duties reasonably intended to benefit those groups; the use of 'person' maintains the broad nondiscrimination scope consistent with statutory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline of student organizations and due process
rubrics_metrics.description: Student organizations are not respondents under the grievance procedures and therefore are not entitled to due process rights under those grievance provisions; recipients must still take appropriate prompt and effective steps to stop or prevent sex discrimination that may affect organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may discipline organizations under their own codes of conduct independent of Title IX procedures. Individuals or groups who believe they were discriminated against may file complaints with OCR for evaluation and potential investigation and resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient responsibility for contractor conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may not absolve themselves of Title IX obligations by delegating operations to contractors, subcontractors, vendors, or others; recipients must provide assurance of non-discrimination and may be required to ensure compliance by third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing regulations (e.g., 34 CFR 106.4(a),(c)) and OCR assurance forms require recipients to ensure contractors do not discriminate. The Department declined to issue categorical guidance about monitoring software applications because applicability depends on facts and context; complaints about contractor conduct can be filed with OCR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection and use of climate surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may collect and disaggregate Title IX-related demographic and complaint data consistent with nondisclosure obligations and other federal, state, and local laws; climate surveys are optional tools recipients may use to assess experiences with sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations do not mandate recipient data collection changes to the CRDC; the Department may solicit comment before changing data collection practices. VAWA 2022 requires the Secretary to develop an online postsecondary survey tool and mandates postsecondary institutions receiving Federal assistance to administer it and publish campus-level results; elementary/secondary schools may adapt the tool. Recipients must respect nondisclosure obligations in § 106.44(j) when disseminating data.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR enforcement practices, remedies, and public information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department's enforcement authority includes suspension or termination of Federal financial assistance and other actions authorized by law; voluntary resolution agreements are an effective enforcement tool, and OCR publishes resolution agreements online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedial actions may include equitable/injunctive relief and financial compensation as necessary. If a recipient fails to comply with a resolution agreement, the Department may initiate administrative proceedings or refer matters to DOJ. OCR's case processing time varies by facts; the Department declined to create a 'safe harbor' for recipients who partially comply, emphasizing the importance of full compliance. OCR maintains a public searchable database of resolution agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of regulatory provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each provision of the final regulations is intended to serve a distinct purpose and operate independently; severability clauses in part 106 continue to apply so that invalidation of one provision should not affect others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble cites precedent and clarifies that specific provisions (e.g., anti-retaliation, application to hostile environment when some conduct occurred outside the program or U.S., grievance procedure requirements) operate separately. The Department included discussion to remove doubt about adopting remaining provisions if any are invalidated.
